description:
Nyxxie's air.1, Spinning Slap: her neutral aerial. She spins a full turn with the phone hand out, slapping around her.

Who she is. Nyxxie, Nyx's fake form (image 1): the same woman as a parody goth e-girl influencer, with a cat-ear headband, huge lashes, fishnets, a pink-and-black pleated skirt, pink-buckled platform boots, a backpack with a ring light on a pole above her left shoulder, and her phone. She never stops moving: loose and bouncy, a show-off who performs for her phone and films herself, and she fights like a brawler. Weight shifts, hip pops, bouncing knees, a toss of the head; overlap and follow-through everywhere.

The phone. She always holds one smartphone in her RIGHT hand, but the rig has no phone mesh yet: keep the right hand closed around an invisible phone the whole clip (fingers curled loosely as around a slim 7 x 15 cm slab, thumb on its face), whatever the arm does. It never changes hands. Her LEFT hand is the free one.

How the game plays it. The match camera sits straight behind her and a little above, so the action must read from behind: gestures out to the side, up or well ahead of her, not hidden in front of her chest. The fighter does not travel in the clip; the game moves her. The game crossfades in and out over about 0.1 s.

This clip is authored slow, at twice the move's game length; the game speeds it up to the move's own ticks. Give every beat its full development: the anticipation, the gesture or hit carried through the hips and shoulders, the follow-through, the settle and the overlap. Never rush a beat.

A forward hit lands on her centre line, well ahead of her chest, not beside her shoulder. After the hit the ending lag is plain: she regains her balance and the arms take the shortest calm path back to the stance. No flourish, no gesture after the hit.

Flow. Generated moves read stiff by default, and for this job the flow check's warnings count as failures. Stagger arrivals (the hips first, then the chest, the arms one or two ticks later, the head last), keep every hold drifting one way by a few degrees, and let the free hand, the fingers and the head trail the main action by one to three ticks (Clip.overlap). Recover in waves.

In the air. The entry reference is a borrowed fall that only sets the frame; tick 0 is free. Her airborne pose, where this clip starts and ends: knees bent and lifted a little, one higher than the other, the phone hand up near her right shoulder, the left arm out for balance, a bounce in her body. There is no floor. The first and last ticks are the same airborne pose.

The clip (72 ticks, played once):
- Tick 0: Her airborne pose.
- Tick 8: Wind: the chest and hips turn 40 degrees to her RIGHT, the phone arm pulled back out to her right, knees tucking.
- Tick 14: Spin (contact): she whips round to her LEFT (counter-clockwise seen from above), the right arm extended at shoulder height, the phone hand sweeping across in front of her on her centre line, about 0.5 m ahead.
- Tick 18: A quarter turn on: the body facing her left, the phone arm trailing.
- Tick 22: Half a turn: her back to the front, the arm out behind her.
- Tick 26: Three quarters: facing her right.
- Tick 32: Finish: the full turn completed, facing front again, the arms opening out, hair flying.
- Tick 44: Unwinding, arms opening and settling.
- Tick 62: Recovered: the airborne pose returning; she can act again.
- Tick 72: Her airborne pose, matching tick 0.

Key the spin at least every quarter turn (ticks 14, 18, 22, 26, 32) so the hips turn the long way round, a full 360 degrees.

fixed: contact at tick 14, active ticks 14-32; the player can act from tick 62
authored at 2x the proposed game length (36 ticks); the game plays it faster, so every beat keeps its proportion
adjustable: small pose details (angles, reach) that keep the sheet pose and the timing
